page.layout: One block of text: a heading "DEDICATIO." at the top, then a running paragraph of full width; below it, at left, a small italic dateline in three lines; at right, the salutation line and signature; a catchword-like mark "IX" at the lower right is a signature-type mark, not text in the main text.

main_text.l: causam me nunc justam satis expósuisse
nem, ut Tuis ad me litteris, quamvis
nique precatus, in quo finio, ut Deus
tem conservet: atque tandem æternùm beet.

l.i: Ultrajecti, ex Museo meo, die VI. Maji anno CIɔ. IƆ. C.I.I.I. Venerandi tui Nominis

page.notes: The page is a dedication ending. The dateline at left is small italic and partly damaged; "Ultrajecti" and "Museo meo, die VI" and the year "MDCLIII" (printed as CIↃ IↃCLIII, read as "clɔ" with damage) are uncertain. The word "beet" is printed as "beet" with a damaged initial, probably "vivat" in the original; read as printed. Several words are partly obscured by specks, including "litteris", "æternùm". Ink spots throughout are not text. The "IX" at lower right is a handwritten or stamped mark and may not be a printed signature.
